note: Both sets cover the same five spanwise curves and share the same duplicated/conflicting pairs (prebend 0 m at r/R=0 twice, pitch-axis 50% at r/R=0 twice, twist 15.5/15 deg at the root, thickness 22/20% at the tip, chord 5.1/5 m at the root). Set A adds a clearly misread point (relative thickness 40% at r/R=0.25, where the curve is about 35%) and a misread twist of 0 deg at r/R=0.6 (curve is still slightly positive there), and its pitch-axis value at r/R=0.6 (30%) is less accurate than Set B's 29%. Set B also gives the closer chord peak (5.8 m near r/R≈0.25 versus A's 5.7 m), so B is the more faithful set overall, though only slightly. Both sets quote subplot captions or bare axis labels that do not support the numeric claims.
remarks: The text layer contains only axis ticks, labels and captions, so every numeric claim comes from reading the plotted curves; small reading differences (e.g. 5.7 vs 5.8 m, 37 vs 38%) are within plot resolution and were not all counted as wrong. Facts both sets miss: relative thickness is about 100% at the root (r/R=0), and the chord maximum is about 5.85 m near r/R≈0.22. Both sets repeat the same facts under near-identical wording (chord/chord length, -2.0/-2 deg, 15.5/15 deg), and several quotes are only subplot labels such as '(a) Chord length' or '(d) Prebend', which cannot support a specific value at a specific span.
